Beginner.learningGoal: Choose between List, Dictionary, HashSet and arrays for everyday tasks.
gotchas: Dictionary indexer throws for a missing key; TryGetValue doesn't
Removing from a List while iterating it with foreach throws
List.Contains is O(n); HashSet.Contains is O(1)
goodSolutionShows: The collection that matches the lookup pattern
TryGetValue / TryAdd instead of double lookups
shapeHints: removing inactive devices from a list

Intermediate.learningGoal: Use specialised collections: Queue, Stack, SortedDictionary, PriorityQueue, LinkedList.
gotchas: PriorityQueue doesn't support updating a priority in place
goodSolutionShows: The right specialised collection with a short justification in code
Readonly views (IReadOnlyCollection) at the API boundary
Correct complexity for the hot operations
shapeHints: a job scheduler ordered by due time

Advanced.learningGoal: Build a custom collection or use frozen/immutable/concurrent collections correctly.
gotchas: FrozenDictionary is fast to read but expensive to create
ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd may run the factory more than once
Implementing IEnumerable<T> without versioning lets callers mutate during enumeration
goodSolutionShows: Collection choice justified by read/write pattern
Lazy<T> or similar where the factory must run once
